text:
Predicates:
InCity(x, y) ::: x is in city y.
InState(x, y) ::: x is in state y.
City(x) ::: x is a city.
State(x) ::: x is a state.
InSameState(x, y) ::: x and y are in the same state.
InDifferentState(x, y) ::: x and y are in different states.

Premises:
City(Billings) ∧ InCity(Billings, Montana) ∧ State(Montana) ∧ InCity(Butte, Montana) ∧ InCity(Helena, Montana) ∧ InCity(Missoula, Montana) ::: Billings is a city in Montana, which includes Butte, Helena, and Missoula.
InCity(WhiteSulphurSprings, Montana) ∧ InCity(Butte, Montana) ::: White Sulphur Springs and Butte are cities in Montana.
InCity(StPierre, NotMontana) ::: St Pierre is not in Montana.
∀x (InCity(x, Butte) → ¬InCity(x, StPierre)) ::: Any city in Butte is not in St Pierre.
∀x ∀y ((InCity(x, y) ∧ City(x) ∧ City(y)) → (InSameState(x, y) ∧ ¬InDifferentState(x, y))) ::: Any city can only be in one state, except for Bristol, Texarkana, Texhoma, and Union City.

Conclusion:
InSameState(StPierre, Bismarck) ::: St Pierre and Bismarck are in the same state.
